items.title: Rail safety plan due November 3 after crash
items.body: Transport Minister Óscar Puente will submit a rail safety plan to cabinet on November 3; several parties demand his resignation. The Urda crash killed 69 people. Experts point to system failures beyond human error. Renfe has ordered a 40 km/h limit when the LZB automatic braking system fails.

items.title: Landlords cannot require tenants to buy rent insurance
items.body: A housing decree in force since October 8 bars landlords from requiring tenants to buy rent non-payment insurance or similar cover. Clauses in contracts signed before that date are not automatically void. Landlords can still buy and pay for the insurance themselves.

items.title: October regulated electricity bill exceeds 80 euros
items.body: A typical household's October bill on the regulated PVPC electricity tariff exceeded 80 euros, up 8% from September and 29% from October 2025. Rising wholesale and gas prices drove the rise, with gas costs linked to war in the Middle East and the situation in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: PP resets election campaign after Urda crash
items.body: The PP is shifting its campaign toward management and experience before the November 29 general election. After suspending events following the Urda crash, it will meet on November 2 without flags or anthems. The party fears the public reaction could boost Vox, which stood at 19% in pre-crash polls.

items.title: Banks charge up to 276 euros yearly for accounts
items.body: CaixaBank and Cajamar charge up to 276 euros a year for an account and debit card when customers meet none of their fee-waiver conditions. Banks increasingly reserve free offers for online customers. Basic payment accounts cost at most 36 euros yearly and are free for the most vulnerable customers.

items.title: Barcelona Halloween police operation sees no incidents by midnight
items.body: Police reported no incidents by midnight during Barcelona's October 31 operation against planned Blocus rallies. Officers identified 1,440 people and made three arrests. The measures included street and metro access closures and the removal of about 200 rubbish containers in central Barcelona.

items.title: Most Madrid housing campers leave Puerta del Sol
items.body: Most groups in Madrid's Puerta del Sol housing camp have left after two warnings from the Government Delegation. The movement will shift to neighbourhoods and support the November 11 general strike. Some campers remain. Congress did not approve the housing decrees the camp forced to a vote.

items.title: Canary Islands researchers study unusually bright cosmic afterglow
items.body: A gamma-ray burst detected on March 10 produced one of the brightest afterglows in 20 years despite a modest initial signal. Research involving the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias suggests Earth's position hid the most intense part of the explosion, linked to a massive star's death.
